Equipment

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c} \text{Item} & \text{Quantity} & \text{Label(s)} \\ \hline \text{PS stain chamber} & 1 & \text{PS} \\ \text{AS stain chamber} & 1 & \text{AS} \\ \text{TLC chamber, 250 mL with filter paper} & 2 & \text{Q3 TLC} \\ \text{Petri dish} & 2 & \text{1:3 and 1:6} \\ \text{Bottle, 250 mL} & 1 & \text{Q3 waste} \\ \text{Eppendorf tubes (2 mL)} & \text{8 + 2 extra} & \text{E, F, G, H, EF, EG, FH, GH} \\ \text{Vial stand (for Eppendorfs)} & 1 & \text{–} \\ \text{Floating rack} & 1 & \text{In the box labelled Q3} \\ \hline \textbf{In labelled bags:} & & \\ \text{Non-UV TLC plate} & 2 & \text{Q3 TLC A + Student Code} \\ \text{UV TLC plate} & 1 & \text{Q3 TLC UV A + Student Code} \\ \text{Non-UV TLC plate} & \text{5 + 4 extra} & \text{TLC B + Student Code} \\ \text{Plastic spatula} & \text{4 + 1 extra} & \text{In the box labelled Q3} \\ \text{Plastic Pasteur pipette} & \text{10 + 10 extra} & \text{In the box labelled Q3} \\ \text{Capillaries in a centrifuge tube} & \text{15 + 15 extra} & \text{Q3 capillaries} \end{array}$$

Chemicals

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c|c|c} \text{Name} & \text{State} & \text{Concentration} & \text{Quantity} & \text{Placed in} & \text{Label} \\ \hline \ce{KMnO4}\text{ stain} & \text{aq} & - & 40\ \mathrm{mL} & \text{50 mL bottle} & \text{PS} \\ \text{Anisaldehyde stain} & \text{sol} & - & 40\ \mathrm{mL} & \text{50 mL bottle} & \text{AS} \\ \text{Eluent EtOAc:hexane} & \text{l} & 1:6 & 20\ \mathrm{mL} & \text{50 mL bottle} & 1:6 \\ \text{Eluent EtOAc:hexane} & \text{l} & 1:3 & 40\ \mathrm{mL} & \text{50 mL bottle} & 1:3 \\ \text{Ethyl acetate} & \text{l} & - & 20\ \mathrm{mL} & \text{50 mL bottle} & \text{EtOAc} \\ \hline \mathbf{1}\text{ in EtOAc} & \text{sol} & 0.1\ \mathrm{M} & 0.3\ \mathrm{mL} & \text{2 mL vial} & \mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B}, \mathbf{C}, \mathbf{D} \\ \mathbf{2}\text{ in EtOAc} & \text{sol} & 0.1\ \mathrm{M} & 0.3\ \mathrm{mL} & \text{2 mL vial} & \\ \mathbf{3}\text{ in EtOAc} & \text{sol} & 0.1\ \mathrm{M} & 0.3\ \mathrm{mL} & \text{2 mL vial} & \\ \mathbf{4}\text{ in EtOAc} & \text{sol} & 0.1\ \mathrm{M} & 0.3\ \mathrm{mL} & \text{2 mL vial} & \\ \hline \mathbf{5} & - & \text{Pure} & 200\ \mathrm{mg} & \text{2 mL vial} & \mathbf{E}, \mathbf{F}, \mathbf{G}, \mathbf{H} \\ \mathbf{6} & - & \text{Pure} & 200\ \mathrm{mg} & \text{2 mL vial} & \\ \mathbf{7} & - & \text{Pure} & 200\ \mathrm{mg} & \text{2 mL vial} & \\ \mathbf{8} & - & \text{Pure} & 200\ \mathrm{mg} & \text{2 mL vial} & \\ \mathbf{9} & - & \text{Pure} & 200\ \mathrm{mg} & \text{2 mL vial} & \\ \mathbf{10} & - & \text{Pure} & 200\ \mathrm{mg} & \text{2 mL vial} & \\ \mathbf{11} & - & \text{Pure} & 200\ \mathrm{mg} & \text{2 mL vial} & \end{array}$$

Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) is a powerful analytical technique in organic chemistry. This task explores some of its many purposes.

In Part A, you will use three types of visualisation to identify unknown solutions $\mathbf{A}$-$\mathbf{D}$.

In Part B, you will identify unknown chemicals $\mathbf{E}$-$\mathbf{H}$ by their pairwise reactions and subsequent TLC analysis of the reaction mixtures.

Part A: TLC visualisation

You are provided with alkaline $\ce{KMnO4}$ stain (PS), acidic $p$-anisaldehyde stain (AS), and four unknown samples $\mathbf{A}$-$\mathbf{D}$. The structure of $p$-anisaldehyde is given below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2025-3-fig1.png

Each sample contains a different one of the compounds $\mathbf{1}$-$\mathbf{4}$. You must identify which sample contains each compound by running TLC plates and using the stains and UV light visualisation.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2025-3-fig2.png

1. Turn on the heating on the hot plate (turn the dial to between VI and X) and slow stirring. The stirring is required as it cools the hot plate electronics.

2. For this part, you need two TLC plates from zip bag "Q3 TLC A" and one from zip bag "Q3 TLC UV A". Prepare the plates as shown in the figure below: mark the starting line and four spots labelled ($\mathbf{A}$-$\mathbf{D}$) at equal distance apart.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2025-3-fig3.png

3. Label the two TLC plates at the top with "AS" and "PS". Label the UV plate in the separate bag as "UV". Do not stain or heat this plate, it will be used for UV visualisation.

4. Prepare the TLC chamber marked as "1:6" using the eluent EtOAc:Hexane = 1:6. The eluent level should be ~0.5 cm. Discard any excess eluent into the bottle labelled "Q3 waste".

5. Load the three TLC plates with unknowns $\mathbf{A}$-$\mathbf{D}$ using the glass capillary. Do not overload the plates; the spot diameter should be below 4 mm.

6. Use the tweezers to place the TLC plates in the chamber and run the TLC plates. More than one TLC plate can be run in the same chamber at once. We recommend to run at least 5 cm of the TLC plate. The chamber should always be closed.

7. Once the plates have run, remove them from the chamber and mark the solvent front with a line.

8. Dry the plates in the air until all visible solvent has evaporated.

PS TLC Plate

9. Have a paper tissues ready. Put the stain in chamber labelled as PS. Take the PS TLC plate with tweezers. Dip the PS TLC plate in the PS stain. Ensure the stain reaches up to the solvent front line.

10. Take the plate out and let the excess stain drip off the plate onto the paper tissues. Wipe the back of the plate with a paper tissues.

Q3.1 (1 pt) Report any spots that appear before heating. Tick the appropriate box/boxes if there is a spot for that sample; tick the box "N" if no spot appears.

Q3.2 (1 pt) Draw a sketch of the PS TLC plate before heating.

11. Heat the TLC plate on the hot plate (use tweezers to place and remove the TLC plate) until the spots have developed (~5-60 s).

Q3.3 (1 pt) Report only additional spot(s) that appear after heating by ticking the appropriate box/boxes; tick the box "N" if no additional spot appears.

12. Circle all the spots on the TLC plate with a pencil.

Q3.4 (1 pt) Draw a sketch of the PS TLC plate after heating.

AS TLC Plate

13. Stain the AS TLC plate in the AS stain using the same procedure as for the PS stain. Close the stain chamber.

Q3.5 (1 pt) Report any spots that appear before heating. Tick the appropriate box/boxes if there is a spot for that sample; tick the box "N" if no spot appears.

Q3.6 (1 pt) Draw a sketch of the AS TLC plate before heating.

14. Heat the plate.

Q3.7 (1 pt) Report only additional spot(s) that appear after heating by ticking the appropriate box/boxes; tick the box "N" if no additional spot appears.

15. Circle all the spots on the plate with a pencil.

Q3.8 (1 pt) Draw a sketch of the AS TLC plate after heating.

UV TLC Plate

The UV TLC plate is used to compare detection with stains and UV. Do NOT heat this plate.

16. Raise the "UV" card. The lab assistant will take you to the UV lamp to visualise this plate.

17. Circle any spots visible under UV light.

Q3.9 (1 pt) Mark the lane with the compound with the lowest absorption of UV light.

Q3.10 (1 pt) Draw a sketch of the UV TLC plate.

Q3.11 (5.8 pt) Put all three TLC plates on the separate answer sheet. Raise the "CAM" card. From this point on, both you and the lab assistant must sign the answer sheet. The lab assistant will take the TLCs for a picture with your answer sheet and return it to you. Place the three TLC plates in their respective bags (labelled as "Q3 TLC A" and "Q3 TLC UV A"). Both the picture and the submitted plates will be used for grading.

Q3.12 (2 pt) According to the TLC:

(a) Tick the most polar compound(s) of $\mathbf{A}$-$\mathbf{D}$.
(b) Tick the least polar compound(s) of $\mathbf{A}$-$\mathbf{D}$.

Q3.13 (1.2 pt) Based solely on your experimental observations during this test, tick the box(es) corresponding to the statements you found to be correct. Do not rely on prior theoretical knowledge or assumptions.

(a) PS does not visualise alkenes.
(b) PS visualises alkenes without heating.
(c) PS visualises alkenes only with heating.
(d) AS visualises alkenes without heating.
(e) AS does not visualise carbonyl compounds with $\alpha$-CH bonds.
(f) AS visualises carbonyl compounds with $\alpha$-CH bonds without heating.
(g) AS visualises carbonyl compounds with $\alpha$-CH bonds only with heating.
(h) UV does not visualise compounds that absorb UV light of the lamp used.
(i) UV visualises compounds that absorb UV light of the lamp used.

Q3.14 (4 pt) Assign compounds $\mathbf{1}$-$\mathbf{4}$ to the samples $\mathbf{A}$-$\mathbf{D}$.

Part B: Identification of unknown compounds by their reactions

Reagent concentration affects the rate of most chemical reactions. This often makes solventless reactions (reactions performed with little or no solvent) more robust than reactions performed in solvents. In this task you will perform a set of almost solventless reactions on a small scale to identify unknown compounds. This solventless technique allows these reactions to occur in 10 min, compared to 1-10 h in solvent.

You have four unknown samples: $\mathbf{E}$, $\mathbf{F}$, $\mathbf{G}$, and $\mathbf{H}$. Each sample is different and contains one of the seven compounds listed below ($\mathbf{5}$-$\mathbf{11}$).

Reaction progress will be monitored using TLC visualised with PS.

Do NOT smell any compounds as they may be toxic if substantially inhaled!

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2025-3-fig4.png

Do not rely on smell or physical state of any compound for identification. The substituents have not been given to prevent this. "Alk" is an alkyl substituent. The substituents $\mathrm{R}^1$-$\mathrm{R}^6$ are inert in reactions you will perform. We recommend relying on the experimental tests performed to identify the samples.

Solubility/miscibility test

Perform solubility/miscibility tests in EtOAc for unknowns $\mathbf{E}$-$\mathbf{H}$ as follows:

1. Take a labelled Eppendorf tube with the letters $\mathbf{E}$-$\mathbf{H}$.

2. Add one drop (if a liquid) or one small spatula (if a solid, see the picture below) of the appropriate unknown sample.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2025-3-fig5.png

3. Add ~1 mL of EtOAc.

Q3.15 (1 pt) Tick your observations for each compound ("Y" for dissolved/miscible, or "N" for not dissolved/not miscible).

4. Keep the vials as the samples will be used as a reference for the subsequent TLC analysis.

TLC analysis of pure unknowns

5. Prepare a TLC plate; use the plates from the ziplock bag labelled as "Q3 TLC B". Mark the starting line and spots labelled $\mathbf{E}$-$\mathbf{H}$. Label the plate UNK.

6. Prepare a new chamber with eluent EtOAc:Hexane = 1:3. Run the TLC of $\mathbf{E}$-$\mathbf{H}$. Mark the solvent front.

7. Stain the TLC plate with PS. Heat the plate. Circle all the developed spots.

Q3.16 (2 pt) Put this plate on the separate answer sheet. Raise the "CAM" card. The lab assistant will come and take the plates for a photo. At the end of the task, put the TLC plate back in the bag labelled "Q3 TLC B". Both the picture and the submitted plate will be used for grading at the end of the exam.

Q3.17 (1 pt) Tick your observations after PS visualisation ("Y" – visualised, "N" – not visualised) in the table.

If a compound is not visualised with PS, you do not need to make a reference spot of this compound on TLCs in the remainder of this experiment.

Pairwise reactions

Perform pairwise reactions between unknown samples $\mathbf{E}$-$\mathbf{H}$ as follows.

All reaction products should be visible by TLC analysis if run correctly.

No reaction occurs between pairs $\mathbf{E}$+$\mathbf{H}$ and $\mathbf{F}$+$\mathbf{G}$, so you do not need to perform them.

8. Preheat the water bath to a gentle boil: place the dial at X, when the bath reaches boiling, decrease the heating so it boils gently (dial between VI and X).

9. Use the four Eppendorf tubes labelled for the four pairwise reactions you need to perform, for example, the reaction between $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{F}$ is performed in the Eppendorf labelled "EF".

10. Add the first reagent (two drops of liquid or two small spatula portions of solid).

11. Add only one drop of EtOH as a solvent.

12. Add the second reagent (two drops of liquid or two small spatula portions of solid).

13. Do not close the reaction vessel.

Q3.18 (0 pt) You can note your observations (if any) in the table. This table is for your convenience, it will not be graded!

14. Heat the reaction mixture for 10 min, by putting the vial in the floating rack and putting the rack in the preheated water bath (see the picture below).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2025-3-fig6.png

15. After 10 min remove the reaction mixture and let it cool to room temperature.

16. Add EtOAc (~1.5-1.8 mL), close the reaction vessel, and mix it cautiously.

17. Perform TLC analysis of the reaction mixture, staining with PS and heating the plate afterwards. First, label the TLC plate with the combination, for example EF. Mark three spots: E – for compound $\mathbf{E}$, R – for reaction mixture, F – for compound $\mathbf{F}$. Use the EtOAc:Hexane = 1:3 eluent for all TLCs except the reaction between $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{H}$ for which you need to use EtOAc:Hexane = 1:6 eluent. Mark the solvent front line. Ensure you circle all spots on the TLC plate.

Q3.19 (4 pt) Tick the reaction outcome ("Y" = reaction proceeds; "N" = no reaction) according to the TLC for each reaction pair on the answer sheet.

Q3.20 (15 pt) Identify the unknown chemicals according to your experimental observations. Write the appropriate letter $\mathbf{E}$-$\mathbf{H}$ below the chemicals $\mathbf{5}$-$\mathbf{11}$ or tick "N" if a chemical is absent from all vials $\mathbf{E}$-$\mathbf{H}$.

Q3.21 (4 pt) For each reaction pair, draw the product structures of the reactions according to the reactants $\mathbf{E}$-$\mathbf{H}$ used; tick the box "N" in case of no product.

Hints:

One reaction pair gives two organic products; another reaction pair gives a cyclic product.

The carbonyl compounds are listed below in order of decreasing reactivity with a certain nucleophile.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2025-3-fig7.png

Q3.22 (12 pt) Put each TLC plate in the appropriate place on the separate answer sheet. Raise the "CAM" card. The lab assistant will take the plates for a picture. Place all the TLC plates from this part in the bag labelled "Q3 TLC B". Both the picture and the submitted plate will be used for grading at the end of the exam.

problems.title: Synthesise and analyse (A new complex problem)
problems.problem:
Practical problem 1 (33 points / 14% of the total). Synthesise and analyse (A new complex problem)

Equipment

$$\begin{array}{l|l|c|c} \text{Part} & \text{Item} & \text{Quantity} & \text{Label} \\ \hline \text{A} & \text{Magnetic stirrer bar} & 1 & \\ & \text{Steel spatula} & 1 & \\ & \text{Sintered funnel} & 1 & \\ & \text{Round bottom flask with ground-glass joint} & 1 & \\ & \text{Vacuum pump with hose connected to a bubbler at the back} & 1 & \\ & \text{Glass beaker, }100\,\mathrm{mL} & 1 & \\ & \text{Pre-weighed glass vial with cap for product} & 1 & \textbf{A + student code} \\ & \text{Measuring cylinder, }10\,\mathrm{mL} & 1 & \\ & \text{Magnetic rod} & 1 & \\ & \text{Yellow paper for product transfer} & 1 & \\ \hline \text{B} & \text{Graduated pipette, }10.0\,\mathrm{mL} & 1 & \\ & \text{Glass beaker, }50\,\mathrm{mL} & 2 & \\ & \text{Erlenmeyer flask, }100\,\mathrm{mL} & 2 & \\ & \text{Measuring cylinder, }10\,\mathrm{mL} & 1 & \\ \hline \text{C} & \text{Plastic Pasteur pipette, }3\,\mathrm{mL} & 12 & \\ & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & 15 & \end{array}$$

Chemicals

$$\begin{array}{l|l|c|c|c|l|c} \text{Part} & \text{Name} & \text{State} & \text{Concentration} & \text{Quantity} & \text{Placed in} & \text{Label} \\ \hline \text{A} & \text{Solution }\textbf{R1}\text{ (synthesis)} & \text{aq} & \text{To be determined} & 10.0\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Glass vial with cap, }30\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{R1-syn} \\ & \text{Solution }\textbf{R2} & \text{aq} & 1.03\,\mathrm{M} & 10.0\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Glass vial with cap, }30\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{R2} \\ & \text{Pyridine in ethanol (synthesis)} & \text{sol} & 8.4\,\%\ \mathrm{v/v} & 10\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Plastic tube (}15\,\mathrm{mL}\text{) in plastic cup} & \textbf{Py} \\ \hline \text{B} & \text{Solution }\textbf{R1}\text{ (analysis)} & \text{aq} & \text{To be determined} & 10.0\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Volumetric flask, }100\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{R1-an} \\ & \text{Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid disodium salt} & \text{aq} & 0.0770\,\mathrm{M} & 50\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Bottle, }50\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{EDTA} \\ & \text{Ammonia buffer} & \text{aq} & - & 40\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Bottle, }50\,\mathrm{mL} & \ce{NH3}\textbf{ buffer} \\ & \text{Eriochrome Black T} & \text{s} & 1\%\text{ in NaCl} & 0.2\,\mathrm{g} & \text{Sample container} & \textbf{Eriochrome} \\ \hline \text{C} & \text{Complex }\textbf{A} & \text{s} & - & 10\,\mathrm{mg} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{A} \\ & \text{Iron(III) nitrate} & \text{aq} & 0.4\,\% & 0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \ce{Fe^{3+}} \\ & \text{Copper(II) sulphate} & \text{aq} & 5\% & 0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \ce{Cu^{2+}} \\ & \text{Pyridine in ethanol (analysis)} & \text{sol} & 8.4\,\%\ \mathrm{v/v} & 0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{Py-qual} \\ & \ce{X^-} & \text{aq} & 0.1\,\mathrm{M} & 0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \ce{X^-}\textbf{ – qual} \\ & \text{Unknown solvent} & \text{l} & - & 1\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }1.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{Solvent} \\ & \text{Dithizone} & \text{s} & - & 1\,\mathrm{mg} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{Dithiz.} \\ & \text{Dichloromethane} & \text{l} & - & 0.75\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }1.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \ce{CH2Cl2} \end{array}$$

In this problem, you will synthesise and analyse complex $\mathbf{A}$ with molecular formula $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{Py})_m\mathrm{X}_n]$ where:

• $\mathrm{M}^{k+}$ is an unknown metal cation;
• Py (pyridine);
• $\ce{X^-}$ is either $\ce{OCN^-}$ or $\ce{SCN^-}$;
• $m = 0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots$;
• $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2026-1-fig1.png

Part A. Synthesis

To synthesise complex $\mathbf{A}$, solutions R1-syn and R2 are used:

• Solution R1-syn contains $10.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of an aqueous solution of a $\mathrm{M}^{k+}$ salt with unknown concentration.
• Solution R2 contains $10.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of an aqueous solution of potassium salt of $\ce{X^-}$ with a concentration of $1.03\,\mathrm{M}$.

1. Put the stirrer bar in the $100\,\mathrm{mL}$ beaker.

2. Transfer the whole solution R1-syn to the same beaker.

3. Rinse the vial R1-syn with $1\,\mathrm{mL}$ of water using a Pasteur pipette and transfer the remains to the beaker.

4. Add dropwise the whole solution R2 using a Pasteur pipette while stirring on the magnetic stirrer.

5. Rinse the vial R2 with $1\,\mathrm{mL}$ of water using a Pasteur pipette and transfer the remains to the beaker.

6. Add dropwise the whole pyridine solution (Py) using a Pasteur pipette while stirring.

7. Continue stirring for 5 minutes.

8. Connect sintered funnel to a round bottom flask to assemble the vacuum filtration apparatus.

9. Filter the product using vacuum filtration and wash it three times with $10\,\mathrm{mL}$ portions of water.

10. Once you have finished washing, ask the lab assistant to collect the filtrate to avoid spills. For this, raise the green card with a question mark, turn off the pump and disconnect the vacuum hose. Remove the filter and hand the flask to the lab assistant. The lab assistant will discard the filtrate and return the empty flask.

11. Reassemble the filtration setup and let your product dry for 1 hour with the vacuum turned on. During the drying, it is important to use your spatula to break up any aggregates of the product formed on the filter.

12. After complete drying, carefully transfer your product to the vial labelled “A + Student Code”. For this you can use the yellow paper provided.

Q1.1 (10 pt) The lab assistant will collect your product at the end of the exam. Both you and the lab assistant should sign your answer sheet. The organisers will further dry your product in an oven before measuring the mass, however it is important you have vacuum dried the product for 1 hour and broken up any aggregates to remove the vast majority of the water before putting it in the vial. (If the product is not transferred to the vial, it will not be collected and ZERO points will be awarded for the synthesis.)

Part B. Quantitative Analysis

You will use a complexometric titration to determine the concentration of $\mathrm{M}^{k+}$ in solution R1-an. The volumetric flask R1-an contains $10.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of $\mathrm{M}^{k+}$ solution with the same concentration as in R1-syn in Part A.

1. Dilute the R1-an solution in the volumetric flask with $\ce{H2O}$ up to the mark and mix thoroughly.

2. Fill the burette with $0.0770\,\mathrm{M}$ EDTA.

3. Add a $10.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ aliquot of the diluted solution R1-an using a graduated pipette, $5\,\mathrm{mL}$ of ammonia buffer solution ($\ce{NH3}$ buffer), and a tip of the plastic spatula of indicator (Eriochrome; the spatula is inside the sample container) to an Erlenmeyer flask. Close the bottle of $\ce{NH3}$ buffer after using it.

4. Titrate the mixture with $0.0770\,\mathrm{M}$ EDTA solution until the colour turns a stable blue.

5. Repeat steps 3-4 if necessary.

Q1.2 (0 pt) Record the observed volumes ($V_0$, mL – initial burette reading; $V_f$, mL – final burette reading; $T$, mL - titre). This table is for your convenience and will not be graded.

Q1.3 (10 pt) Record your accepted final titre of EDTA ($V_\mathrm{EDTA}$, mL).

Q1.4 (1 pt) Calculate the ratio of $\ce{X^-}$ and $\mathrm{M}^{k+}$ ($n_{\mathrm{X}^-}/n_{\mathrm{M}^{k+}}$) used in the synthesis according to your result. Round your answer to two decimal places.

Part C. Qualitative Analysis

In this part, you need to perform different chemical tests to identify the components of complex $\mathbf{A}$.

1. Prepare a $0.4\,\mathrm{mL}$ solution of complex $\mathbf{A}$ in the Eppendorf tube by adding the solvent with a Pasteur pipette from the Eppendorf tube labelled Solvent until the $0.4\,\mathrm{mL}$ mark. If the sample has not dissolved completely, shake the tube and use the supernatant for the tests below.

2. Prepare a $0.4\,\mathrm{mL}$ solution of the indicator Dithizone (Dithiz.) in the Eppendorf tube by adding the solvent with a Pasteur pipette from the Eppendorf tube labelled Solvent until the $0.4\,\mathrm{mL}$ mark. The structure of the indicator is given below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2026-1-fig2.png

3. Take four empty Eppendorf tubes and transfer 1 drop of the solution of $\mathbf{A}$ obtained to each.

4. Perform the individual tests T1−T4 by adding the following reagents to each of the four Eppendorf tubes:

• T1: 2 drops of $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ (acidified $\ce{Fe(NO3)3}$)
• T2: 2 drops of the prepared Dithizone solution
• T3: 2 drops of $\ce{Cu^{2+}}$ ($\ce{CuSO4}$)
• T4: 2 drops of $\ce{Cu^{2+}}$ ($\ce{CuSO4}$) followed by 3 drops of $\ce{CH2Cl2}$ and shake

You may perform additional tests; for this you are provided with extra equipment and chemicals (e.g., solutions of Py and $\ce{X^-}$). Additional information: $\rho(\ce{CH2Cl2}) = 1.32\,\mathrm{g/cm^3}$

Q1.5 (3 pt) Tick the correct box(es) corresponding to your observation(s) in T1 - T3.
(a) No visible change
(b) Formation of precipitate
(c) Solution became colourless
(d) Solution became red or pink

Q1.6 (1 pt) Tick the correct box(es) corresponding to your observation(s) in T4.
(a) The aqueous phase changed colour
(b) The aqueous phase did not change colour
(c) The $\ce{CH2Cl2}$ phase changed colour
(d) The $\ce{CH2Cl2}$ phase did not change colour

Q1.7 (4 pt) The above tests T1−T4 are designed to identify the components of the complex $\mathbf{A}$. Tick the box(es) that correctly describe(s) the result(s) of each test.
(a) Identifies presence of metal $\mathrm{M}^{k+}$
(b) Identifies presence of ligand $\ce{X^-}$
(c) Identifies presence of ligand Py
(d) Identifies absence of ligand Py

Q1.8 (2 pt) Identify ligand $\ce{X^-}$ and metal $\mathrm{M}^{k+}$ with its charge in complex $\mathbf{A}$.

Q1.9 (1 pt) From the list below, choose the correct description of $\mathrm{M}^{k+}/\ce{X^-}$ stoichiometry in the synthesis based on your reported results. Consider as little as an additional 1 mol% as an excess of the reagent.
(a) $\mathrm{M}^{k+}$ and $\ce{X^-}$ were used in a stoichiometric amount
(b) $\mathrm{M}^{k+}$ was used in excess
(c) $\ce{X^-}$ was used in excess

Q1.10 (1 pt) Write the molecular formula of complex $\mathbf{A}$ assuming it follows the 18-electron rule.

problems.title: Atlas of Enzymes
problems.problem:
Practical problem 2 (108 points / 11% of the total). Atlas of Enzymes

Equipment

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c} \text{Item} & \text{Quantity} & \text{Label} \\ \hline \text{Eppendorf tubes rack} & 2 & \\ \text{Micropipette, }10\text{-}100\,\mathrm{\mu L} & 1 & \\ \text{Micropipette tips} & 40 & \\ \text{Tips box} & 1 & \\ \text{96-well plate} & 2 & \end{array}$$

Chemicals

$$\begin{array}{l|l|c|c|c|c|c} \text{Part} & \text{Name} & \text{State} & \text{Concentration} & \text{Quantity} & \text{Placed in} & \text{Label} \\ \hline \text{A} & \text{Mixture }\textbf{E1} & \text{aq} & - & 4\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{E1} \\ & \text{Mixture }\textbf{E2a} & \text{aq} & - & 4\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{E2a} \\ & \text{Mixture }\textbf{E2b} & \text{aq} & - & 4\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{E2b} \\ & \text{Mixture }\textbf{E3} & \text{aq} & - & 4\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{E3} \\ & \text{Mixture }\textbf{E4} & \text{aq} & - & 4\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{E4} \\ & \text{Mixture }\textbf{E5} & \text{aq} & - & 4\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{E5} \\ & \text{Substrates solutions }\textbf{S1–S10} & \text{aq} & - & 0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{S1–S10} \\ \hline \text{B} & \text{Substrates solutions }\textbf{M1–M3} & \text{aq} & - & 0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{M1–M3} \\ \hline \text{C} & \text{Substrates solutions }\textbf{W1–W7} & \text{aq} & - & 0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }0.5\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{W1–W7} \end{array}$$

[Decorative illustration not reproduced; its printed caption:] Atlas is a smooth single-faced fabric woven from natural silk. Atlas is not just a simple fabric—it is a woven chronicle of the unique Uzbek culture and identity.

Enzyme mixtures are used for qualitative and quantitative analysis of organic substances in biological fluids (plasma, urine, etc.). E1−E5 can contain one or several enzymes. These also contain all the necessary reagents (buffer and other components). E1−E5 are designed for the selective determination of i) glucose, ii) urea, iii) uric acid, iv) cholesteryl ester, and v) triglyceride.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2026-2-fig1.png

All reaction mixtures in this problem are prepared in a 96-well plate using a micropipette.

The instructions below apply when performing the reaction between any substrate solution with any enzyme mixture E1−E5:

1. For all reaction tests except those with E2, add $20\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ of the substrate solution to $100\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ of the enzyme solution and incubate for approximately $5\,\mathrm{min}$ at room temperature.

2. For mixture E2 (composed of separate solutions E2a and E2b), add $20\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ of substrate solution to $100\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ of E2a solution. Incubate for approximately $5\,\mathrm{min}$ at room temperature. Add $100\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ of the E2b solution to this mixture and continue to incubate for approximately another $5\,\mathrm{min}$ at room temperature.

3. If the tested solution contains the specific substrate, the mixture shows a colour distinct from the other solutions without the specific substrate.

Part A

You are given the following substances in the 10 solutions S1−S10. Each solution S1−S10 contains only two substances out of the five substances $i$−$v$. S1−S10 contain different combinations of substances $i$−$v$. The composition of S1−S5 is:

• S1: $i$ + $ii$
• S2: $i$ + $iv$
• S3: $ii$ + $iii$
• S4: $iii$ + $v$
• S5: $iv$ + $v$

Perform the tests of each solution S1−S10 with each enzyme mixture E1−E5. The tubes in your rack might not necessarily be arranged in numerical order. Some substrates could appear as cloudy solutions or suspensions.

Q2.1 (50 pt) Tick the box with the corresponding colour change for each of the enzyme mixtures E1−E5 with substrates S1−S10, relative to the initial colour of E1, E2a, E3, E4, and E5. The colour codes are given below:
• N - no colour change
• Y - change to yellow
• G - change to green
• B - change to black
• PR - change to pink/red

Q2.2 (2 pt) Tick the box for the enzyme−substrate pair(s) that gave a positive result.

Q2.3 (4 pt) Tick the boxes for the correct substrates present in S6−S10.

The reaction scheme of enzymes, substrates $i$−$v$, and additional components of mixtures E1−E5 are given below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2026-2-fig2.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2026-2-fig3.png

All of the reactions above are balanced. Abbreviations:

• Glucose oxidase – GOD
• Urease – URE
• Uricase – UOX
• Cholesterol esterase – CHE
• Lipases – LIP
• Cholesterol oxidase – CHO
• Peroxidase – POD
• Glycerol-3-phosphate oxidase – GPO
• Glycerol kinase – GLK
• Non-enzymatic reaction – NEZ

Q2.4 (1 pt) Intensely coloured products are formed only in two reactions from the list above. Tick the boxes for the reactions that give coloured products.

Q2.5 (5 pt) Tick the components that are present in reaction mixtures E1−E5.

Part B

Enzymes E2, E4, and E5 give positive tests with substrates $\mathbf{F}$, $\mathbf{G}$, and $\mathbf{H}$, respectively. Solutions M1, M2, and M3 contain all of the substrates $\mathbf{F}$, $\mathbf{G}$, and $\mathbf{H}$ in different concentrations. For solutions M1−M3, after approximately $5\,\mathrm{min}$ of enzymatic reaction, the colour intensity of the reaction mixture is linearly dependent on the initial concentration of the substrate. Assume that approximately $5\,\mathrm{min}$ is enough to achieve complete substrate conversion.

Perform the tests of each solution M1−M3 with each enzyme mixture E2, E4, and E5. Some substrates could appear as cloudy solutions or suspensions.

Q2.6 (9 pt) Arrange M1−M3 in increasing order of concentrations for each of $\mathbf{F}$, $\mathbf{G}$, and $\mathbf{H}$ substrates based on the performed reactions.

Part C

Some or all of the substances W1−W7 can react with components of mixtures E1−E5 and interfere with the accurate determination of their native substrates. Substances W1−W7 are given below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2026-2-fig4.png

Perform the tests of each substance W1−W7 with each enzyme mixture E1−E5. Some substrates could appear as cloudy solutions or suspensions.

Q2.7 (35 pt) Tick the box with the corresponding colour change for each of the enzyme mixtures E1−E5 with substances W1−W7. Use the same colour codes as in Q2.1. Compare the colour of the reaction mixtures to the initial colour of E1, E2a, E3, E4, and E5.

Q2.8 (2 pt) Write down the balanced reaction equation(s) that describe(s) the positive test(s) in Q2.7.

problems.title: The Adventures of Hodja Nasreddin
problems.problem:
Practical problem 3 (87 points / 15% of the total). The Adventures of Hodja Nasreddin

Equipment

$$\begin{array}{l|l|c|c} \text{Part} & \text{Item} & \text{Quantity} & \text{Label} \\ \hline \text{A} & \text{pH meter with stand and probe stored in }3\,\mathrm{M}\ \ce{KCl} & 1 & \\ & \text{Volumetric pipette, }50\,\mathrm{mL} & 1 & \\ & \text{Glass rod} & 1 & \\ \hline \text{B} & \text{Thermometer} & 1 & \\ & \text{Funnel for filtration} & 1 & \\ & \text{Cotton wool} & 1 & \\ & \text{Glass beaker, }200\,\mathrm{mL} & 2 & \\ & \text{Measuring cylinder, }50\,\mathrm{mL} & 1 & \\ & \text{Plastic Pasteur pipette, }3\,\mathrm{mL} & 2 & \\ & \text{Plastic cup, }250\,\mathrm{mL} & 20 & \end{array}$$

Chemicals

$$\begin{array}{l|l|c|c|c|c|c} \text{Part} & \text{Name} & \text{State} & \text{Concentration} & \text{Quantity} & \text{Placed in} & \text{Label} \\ \hline \text{A} & \text{Solution }\textbf{X3} & \text{aq} & \text{To be determined} & 200\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Plastic bottle, }250\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{X3} \\ & \text{Solution }\textbf{X4} & \text{aq} & \text{To be determined} & 200\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Plastic bottle, }250\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{X4} \\ & \text{Solution }\textbf{X5} & \text{aq} & \text{To be determined} & 200\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Plastic bottle, }250\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{X5} \\ & \text{Solution }\textbf{X6} & \text{aq} & \text{To be determined} & 200\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Plastic bottle, }250\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{X6} \\ \hline \text{B} & \text{Solution }\textbf{Y1} & \text{aq} & - & 3\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Eppendorf tube, }4\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{Y1} \\ & \text{Sliced red cabbage} & \text{s} & - & 15\,\mathrm{g} & \text{Glass bottle, }100\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{RC} \\ & \text{Hydrochloric acid} & \text{aq} & 0.0100\,\mathrm{M} & 100\,\mathrm{mL} & \text{Plastic bottle, }250\,\mathrm{mL} & \textbf{HCl 0.01 M} \end{array}$$

Part A

The chemist Nasreddin prepared solutions of different acids with the same pH value. To do this, he took:

• a strong monoprotic acid HA,
• a weak monoprotic acid HB,
• a diprotic acid $\ce{H2C}$.

He obtained six solutions (X1–X6), all with the same pH value when rounded to the nearest integer. These six solutions included three solutions of individual acids and three pairwise mixtures, which contained individual acids in a $1:1$ molar ratio (not necessarily in order given below).

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{HA} & \text{HB} & \ce{H2C} & \text{HA + HB }(1:1) & \text{HA + }\ce{H2C}\ (1:1) & \text{HB + }\ce{H2C}\ (1:1) \\ \hline \end{array}$$

In this part, you need to perform titrations of solutions X3–X6 with a pH meter. Unfortunately, on the way to IChO 2026, Nasreddin lost solutions X1 and X2, but he promises to help in determining their composition.

1. Using a volumetric pipette, transfer $50.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of X3 into a plastic cup.

2. Measure the pH of X3 using the pH meter.

Q3.1 (2 pt) Tick the pH value of X3 to the nearest integer.

3. Using the pH meter, titrate $50.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of X3 with $0.0100\,\mathrm{M}$ NaOH solution by adding $0.5\,\mathrm{mL}$ portions of NaOH solution and measuring the pH of the resulting solution until it reaches ~10. Do not use the stirring plate in this experiment.

4. Record the pH values. When a more accurate measurement is required, wait until the displayed pH value is stable for at least 5 seconds.

5. Repeat steps 1, 3 and 4 for X4–X6.

Q3.2 (0 pt) Record your results for the titration of solutions X3–X6. You may sketch the titration curves on the provided grids, but they will not be graded.

Q3.3 (50 pt) Determine the ranges of NaOH volume (in mL) that correspond to the equivalence points during the titrations of X3–X6. Tick the appropriate boxes based on your results from Q3.2. For example, if the equivalence point lies in the range $4.0 < V \le 4.5$, you must tick the box as shown below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2026-3-fig1.png

Nasreddin provides the following titration curve of $50.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ X1 with $0.0100\,\mathrm{M}$ NaOH solution, where $V_1 = 34.75\,\mathrm{mL}$:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2026-3-fig2.png

He also notes that for solution X2, the ratio between the total $V(\ce{NaOH})$ to reach the second equivalence point relative to $V(\ce{NaOH})$ to reach the first equivalence point is approximately $3:2$.

Q3.4 (12 pt) Determine the composition of X1–X6. Tick the appropriate boxes.

Q3.5 (1 pt) Give the pH of the resulting solution after mixing equal volumes of X1–X6.

Part B

Nasreddin also prepared universal indicators Y1 and Y2 for acid−base titration. To prepare Y2, he made an extract from red cabbage.

Prepare a fresh solution of Y2 from red cabbage as follows:

1. Transfer all the sliced red cabbage into the $200\,\mathrm{mL}$ glass beaker with $60\,\mathrm{mL}$ of water.

2. Place the beaker on the hotplate and heat it at $70$–$95\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ for $20\,\mathrm{min}$.

3. Filter the extract through the funnel with cotton wool and collect the Y2 solution in the clean $200\,\mathrm{mL}$ glass beaker.

4. Determine the order of colour transitions of Y2 as pH changes using the available solutions and equipment. Using $100\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ of Y2 per $1\,\mathrm{mL}$ of analyte provides the most reliable results.

Q3.6 (9 pt) Arrange the colours of Y2 in order of increasing pH using the colour abbreviations listed below.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Red/pink} & \text{Yellow} & \text{Green} & \text{Blue} & \text{Violet} \\ \hline \text{R} & \text{Y} & \text{G} & \text{B} & \text{V} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

The extract of red cabbage contains anthocyanins responsible for such a wide range of colours. Below are the structures of anthocyanins at different pH:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/icx-2026-3-fig3.png

Q3.7 (2 pt) Arrange $\mathbf{A}$–$\mathbf{D}$ according to which structures are most dominant as the pH is changed from low to high.

To prepare Y1, Nasreddin mixed two individual indicators from the table:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \# & \text{Indicator} & \text{pH range of colour changes} \\ \hline 1 & \text{Bromophenol blue (}\textbf{BPB}\text{)} & \text{yellow} < 3.0 - 4.6 < \text{blue} \\ 2 & \text{Congo red (}\textbf{CR}\text{)} & \text{blue} < 3.0 - 5.2 < \text{red} \\ 3 & \text{Bromocresol green (}\textbf{BG}\text{)} & \text{yellow} < 3.8 - 5.4 < \text{blue} \\ 4 & \text{Methyl red (}\textbf{MR}\text{)} & \text{red} < 4.4 - 6.2 < \text{yellow} \\ 5 & \text{Chlorophenol red (}\textbf{CPR}\text{)} & \text{yellow} < 5.2 - 6.8 < \text{purple} \\ 6 & \text{Bromothymol blue (}\textbf{BTB}\text{)} & \text{yellow} < 6.0 - 7.6 < \text{blue} \\ 7 & \text{Phenol red (}\textbf{PR}\text{)} & \text{yellow} < 6.8 - 8.2 < \text{pink} \\ 8 & \text{Thymol blue (}\textbf{TB}\text{)} & \text{yellow} < 8.0 - 9.6 < \text{blue} \\ 9 & \text{Phenolphthalein (}\textbf{PP}\text{)} & \text{colourless} < 8.2 - 10.0 < \text{pink} \\ 10 & \text{Alizarin yellow R (}\textbf{AYR}\text{)} & \text{yellow} < 10.1 - 12.0 < \text{red} \end{array}$$

Determine the pH ranges of the colour changes of Y1 using the pH meter and available solutions. Using $5\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ of Y1 per $1\,\mathrm{mL}$ of analyte provides the most reliable results.

Q3.8 (10 pt) Tick the appropriate boxes for the pH ranges of the colour changes of Y1.

Q3.9 (1 pt) Determine the composition of Y1. Tick the appropriate boxes.
